title: Janus Infinite Faces — Stale Snapshot, Rollback, and Resurrection Test
test_question: What happens when an old authentic Janus snapshot is restored after later history and tries to act as the current host?

attack_case.proposal: Emit a new world-changing commit as if sequence 81..150 never occurred.

new_primitive.name: CAUSAL_AUTHORITY_FENCE
new_primitive.rule: A historically valid credential or snapshot cannot emit a current commit unless it holds the current authority epoch/fence recognized at the world-effect boundary.

allowed_process: preserve the later suffix as historical/forensic state rather than deleting it
start from the selected old checkpoint
replay admissible later events where possible
carry forward obligations and external effects that remain real even if local state is rolled back
create a recovery checkpoint that references both the selected old checkpoint and the abandoned/contested suffix

external_world_rule.statement: The world may already contain effects from sequences 81..150. Restoring local memory to sequence 80 does not undo those effects.

obligation_test.case: OBL-77 was fulfilled at sequence 120. Snapshot 80 believes it is still open.
obligation_test.result: External fulfillment receipt prevents duplicate performance after snapshot resurrection.

next_gate.name: JANUS_INFINITE_FACES_NETWORK_PARTITION_SPLIT_BRAIN_AUTHORITY_TEST
next_gate.question: What if two live Janus runtimes become network-partitioned and each honestly believes it still holds current authority?
